items.title: Fed expected to hold rates steady this week despite hot inflation — but signal they're not done hiking
items.excerpt: The Federal Reserve heads into its interest-rate decision this week facing hotter inflation, keeping the meeting live even as markets widely expect the central bank to hold interest rates steady just days before the midterm elections. ... "This is a perfect time for clear forward guidance that doesn't quite say, but strongly hints, we're pausing now, but we stand ready to raise again and even give a hint that the next meeting might be the next interest rate hike." ... Inflation heated up in September, as the Consumer Price Index accelerated to 3.7% from a year earlier. Core CPI, which excludes food and energy, ticked up to 2.6%, while wholesale prices jumped more than 6%, and the Fed's preferred inflation gauge — the core Personal Consumption Expenditures index — is projected to top 3%. In his last remarks before this week's policy meeting, many observers think Warsh underscored what Fed Vice Chair Philip Jefferson and New York Fed president John Williams previously said: that despite hot inflation reports, they would like to take time to review the data as they consider the prospect of further rate hikes. Warsh neither endorsed nor pushed back on his colleagues' recent signals that they'd like to wait for more data, but he noted that the world had "broadly conformed to our expectations" since the Fed's September meeting. ... After raising rates for the first time in more than three years in September, minutes from that meeting read that most participants assessed that another increase would likely be appropriate by year-end. ... The Fed's benchmark rate is currently in the range of 3.75% to 4%. Traders are pricing in nearly 90% odds it will hold next week, but see 70% odds of a quarter-point hike in December.

items.title: US Business Activity Keeps Fed Inflation Pressure High
items.excerpt: WASHINGTON — U.S. business activity remained firmly in expansion territory in October even as growth cooled slightly from September, while companies raised selling prices at the fastest pace in more than four years. The combination of strong demand and persistent pricing power gives the Federal Reserve another reason to remain cautious as policymakers prepare for their Oct. 27-28 meeting. ... The latest US business activity data show an economy that is still growing quickly enough to generate inflation pressure. S&P Global’s flash Composite PMI slipped to 57.6 from 58.4 in September, while its output-price index climbed to 59.8, the highest reading since August 2022. ... The inflation signal in the survey is more concerning than the slight cooling in headline activity. Businesses across both manufacturing and services reported raising output prices more aggressively, suggesting that higher input costs are being passed through to customers rather than absorbed entirely in profit margins. The output-price index rose to 59.8 from 58.4 in September. Input costs eased slightly to 64.9 from 65.9, but they remain historically elevated, especially for manufacturers exposed to energy, transportation and imported materials. ... American News Brief reported that consumer inflation accelerated to 3.7% in September as gasoline prices and other costs increased. The October PMI now suggests that businesses may be adding another layer of price pressure by passing more of their own expenses through to buyers. ... Energy-market disruptions linked to the Iran conflict remain an important source of pressure. Higher fuel and freight costs can spread from transportation into manufacturing, wholesale distribution and services, increasing the risk that an external oil shock becomes embedded in broader inflation. ... ## Fed Is Expected to Hold Rates Steady Next Week ... Despite the inflation warning, most economists do not expect the Federal Reserve to raise rates at its October meeting. A Reuters poll found that 94 of 100 economists expect the Fed to keep the federal funds target at 3.75% to 4.00% on Oct. 27-28, while all respondents expected another increase in December. ... The survey may be more important for December than for next week’s decision. If the Fed pauses in October, another month of elevated inflation, strong business demand and resilient hiring could strengthen the argument for a year-end increase. ... For consumers, the concern is that inflation pressure is migrating beyond gasoline and other directly visible energy costs. If service providers and manufacturers continue raising prices because demand remains strong, households could face another period in which wage gains struggle to keep up with everyday expenses. ... US business activity therefore presents the Fed with an uncomfortable combination heading into next week’s meeting. The economy remains resilient enough to grow, but that same resilience is helping companies raise prices, increasing the chance that inflation stays above target and that monetary policy remains tight well into 2027.

items.title: California election officials frustrated, rattled by DOJ demand to sequester 'noncitizen' ballots | PBS News
items.excerpt: LOS ANGELES (AP) — Local election officials across California are confused and frustrated after receiving letters from President Donald Trump's Justice Department demanding that county registrars sequester ballots that the federal government believes were sent to noncitizen voters ahead of the midterm elections. The letters, which were sent on Friday, ask for sensitive information, including Social Security numbers, on roughly 20,000 voters. It is illegal for noncitizens to register to vote or cast a ballot. The administration has insisted that immigrants voting is a major problem nationwide, when in fact it is quite rare, as even its own investigations have shown. "All of this is simply meant to raise huge doubts about the integrity of this election," said John Tuteur, the registrar of voters for Napa County in California's wine country. ... The federal government set a 48-hour deadline to provide information, and it warned that legal action could be taken against any official who knowingly counted a noncitizen's vote. ... The letters are the latest escalation in a legal battle between Democratic-dominated California and Trump's Department of Justice ahead of the midterms. The federal government sued on Oct. 15, roughly three weeks before elections, asking a judge to bar the state from counting mail-in ballots from people the federal government has identified as likely noncitizens. A panel of 9th Circuit appeals court judges will hear arguments on Sunday about whether California can be compelled to comply with the federal government's demands. ## Some clerks say they will proceed with counting ballots

Venezuela's opposition leader Machado returns after months in exile, as doubts over democracy deepen CARACAS, Venezuela (AP) — Nobel laureate María Corina Machado has reappeared in Venezuela for the first time since December. She announced her return on social media, saying, “I am here. With you.” Opposition leader Edmundo Gonzalez confirmed her arrival and expressed support. He emphasized the importance of her return for Venezuelans. Machado's homecoming comes amid growing concerns about Venezuela's democratic future. Since the U.S. military deposed Nicolás Maduro, acting President Delcy Rodríguez has led the country. Rodríguez, a Maduro ally, has exceeded her authorized term, and no election is scheduled. Ukraine disputes Elon Musk's claim that its military violated Starlink's terms of service KYIV, Ukraine (AP) — Ukrainian officials have disputed Elon Musk's claims that their military violated Starlink’s terms by using it for offensive drone strikes. A defense adviser to President Zelenskyy says restrictions on Starlink in Ukraine make such use impossible. Earlier this month, Ukrainian drones lost connectivity at high speeds, disrupting air defenses. Officials say the issue was resolved Saturday. Musk acknowledges SpaceX throttled Starlink, stating it was never meant for offensive use. The U.S. government controls changes to Starshield, the military-grade version. Meanwhile, Zelenskyy reports Russia launched nearly 2,300 drones targeting Ukrainian cities last week. Trump's midterm swing brings him to Michigan as Republicans aim to undermine El-Sayed in Senate race PORT HURON, Mich. (AP) — President Donald Trump's busy midterm campaign schedule is bringing him to Michigan, where Republicans hope to claim an open Senate seat on Election Day. Trump is in Port Huron on Sunday to campaign for Mike Rogers, a former congressman. Democrat Abdul El-Sayed would be the first Muslim senator if elected. Trump on Sunday told reporters that “we don't want to see a jihadist senator.” El-Sayed has repeatedly disavowed unproven claims by Republicans that he is connected to the Muslim Brotherhood. El-Sayed has dared Trump to come to Michigan, believing an appearance by the president could backfire on Rogers, given voters' frustration with the economy and the war with Iran. Polls closed in Serbia's election where strongman Vucic is facing student protest movement BELGRADE, Serbia (AP) — Polls have closed in Serbia, where voters cast ballots in a parliamentary election seen as a showdown between strongman leader Aleksandar Vucic and a student-led movement. The election is shaping up as a referendum between Vucic's right-wing party and the Students' List.

items.excerpt: The beloved children's musician Raffi continues to charm audiences with his timeless songs. Fifty years after his debut children's album, his music remains a staple for young children. Raffi's latest album, “Love is Everywhere,” comes out Friday. It features songs celebrating everything from individuality to the importance of voting. He believes that while technology changes, the essence of childhood remains the same. In an interview with The Associated Press, Raffi emphasized the importance of protecting children's development from excessive technology. He also discussed his commitment to not exploiting children through advertising and how it caused him to turn down a movie offer for “Baby Beluga.” NASHVILLE, Tenn. (AP) — Country Music Hall of Famer John Anderson has died at age 71. His family announced his death Wednesday on his social media accounts. Anderson was known for his high, yearning vocal style and hits such as “Swingin’,” “Wild and Blue,” and “Black Sheep.” Born in Apopka, Florida, he moved to Nashville, Tennessee, after high school. He worked odd jobs before his commercial breakthrough in 1977. Anderson was a “New Traditionalist,” sometimes compared to George Jones and Merle Haggard. He was inducted into the Country Music Hall of Fame in 2024 and won two Country Music Association awards. LOS ANGELES (AP) — Jay-Z once called John Legend “our voice,” but Pharrell Williams had a different idea for Legend's baritone. On his new album, “Muse,” Legend dials back his powerhouse vocals, opting for a more conversational delivery at Williams’ urging. The album, out Friday, marks Legend’s first full collaboration with Williams after more than 20 years of friendship. Recorded mostly at Williams’ studio in Paris, it grew from Legend’s appearance on Clipse’s “The Birds Don’t Sing.” In an interview, Legend discussed Williams’ influence, Jay-Z’s compliment and composing his first original stage score for a new musical.

items.title: HYBE Cine Fest 2026 Cinema Event Going Global With 2 Live BTS Broadcasts
items.excerpt: The HYBE Cine Fest is going international this year with a weeklong global event hitting theaters in more than 60 territories from Oct. 24-31. After launching in Latin America in 2024 and expanding to Asia in 2025, this year’s collaboration between Trafalgar Releasing and HYBE will feature six different events, including the first-ever airings of two BTS live broadcasts from South America. The BTS WORLD TOUR ‘ARIRANG’ in Buenos Aires: Live Viewing in cinemas will mark the K-pop supergroup’s first-ever performance in Argentina, with screenings slated for Oct. 24 in the Americas and Oct. 25 in the rest of the world. A second BTS show, ARIRANG in SÃO PAULO: Live Viewing, will mark the grand finale of the boy band’s Latin American tour, with screenings slated for Oct. 30 in the Americas and Oct. 31 in the rest of the world. ... The program will also feature screenings of SEVENTEEN’s WORLD TOUR ‘NEW_’ concert film marking the group’s 10th anniversary, as well as TOMORROW X TOGETHER’s ACT : TOMORROW from that band’s fourth world tour. The programming will including a screening of the Seoul kick-off of ENHYPEN’S BLOOD SAGA WORLD TOUR and a HYBE Cheering Party (in 3D) where fans are encouraged to chant and sing along to 3D-enhanced on-screen lyrics and wave their official light sticks to music videos of their favorite HYBE acts (LE SSERAFIM, &TEAM, BOYNEXTDOOR, TWS, ILLIT, KATSEYE, aoen, CORTIS and SANTOS BRAVOS).
